clue.text: Lies endlessly about soft food

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed around the next piece
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: porkies is British slang for lies
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a spongy dish is constantly lied about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PORKIES to PORKIE; 'about' puts P inside it. A pork pie is a classic British cold savoury pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a savoury pastry filled with meat, an example of something eaten.

clue.text: One sending letters to China?

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a correspondent who writes to a friend abroad

explanation.walkthrough: China seems to be the country; in cockney rhyming slang 'china' (china plate) means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend made through regular correspondence, often overseas, who exchanges letters.

clue.text: Ease off religious education ahead of Christian period

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education
Lent is the season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A teacher eases off the scripture lessons before a fasting season.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or become less severe, to give way.

clue.text: Hit with bars — the cause of being in stitches?

definitions.text: the cause of being in stitches?

parts.note: punch means hit
lines and bars are both stripes or rows

explanation.surface: A boxer hits someone with metal bars, causing wounds that need stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: Stitches seem surgical; 'in stitches' means laughing helplessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line of a joke delivers the laugh that leaves an audience in fits.

clue.text: Heap praise on former lover, upsetting group

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in a down answer, upsetting turns the word upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Someone gushes about an old flame, annoying their circle of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify enthusiastically.

clue.text: Fighting vessel was going round river with it

indicators.note: the word was encircles the following letter

parts.note: hip means fashionable, up to date, with it

explanation.surface: A combat ship once circled a river, carrying something along.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval ship built for combat is a vessel designed for fighting.

clue.text: Item of clothing from week at Ascot, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy means imagine or invent, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone muses on an outfit to wear during race week at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I think'; the I is fodder. Ascot is a famous English racecourse with a smart dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless garment worn over a shirt, often as part of a three-piece suit.

clue.text: Rake to agitate small leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so this letter goes out of the word

parts.note: rouse means stir up or agitate

explanation.surface: A gardener uses a rake to stir up a few fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Rake and leaves suggest gardening; 'Rake' is a libertine and 'leaves' means departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man, a debauchee.

clue.text: Anger with his criminal trials

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's rage leads to criminal trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Court cases where evidence is heard are called this, a sense of judicial proceedings.

clue.text: City play, avoiding Arsenal's first trap

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out a letter
the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A football tale: a city side's tactics avoid falling into Arsenal's trap.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club. 'Trap' looks like a snare; it is slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a port city in Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: Sample of any longer material

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swatch of fabric that has lasted longer than any other.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, an example of material used for clothing.

clue.text: Flower feeder?

parts.note: read flower as something that flows, a river; a stream feeding into a river is what is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom, so a feeder sounds like plant food; read it as flow-er, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream that joins and supplies water to a larger river feeds that river.

clue.text: Finish off a linen hat I fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A milliner boasts of the linen hat they made, meaning to finish off a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: To annihilate is to destroy completely, to kill or wipe out an opponent.

clue.text: Make fun of flipping old pen

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease or make fun of them

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an ancient writing instrument that keeps flipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but it reverses RIB to BIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint, named after its inventor László Bíró, a writing implement.

clue.text: Famous Beetle car shot by Disney initially

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are rearranged
initially means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen Beetle filmed by Disney became a star, as in Herbie.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means renowned, widely acclaimed.

clue.text: Coin a phrase to describe an octet?

definitions.meaning: an old Spanish silver dollar of pirate lore

definitions.text: a phrase to describe an octet?
definitions.meaning: an octet is a group of eight, so any one member is literally a part of eight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin a phrase' reads as the idiom for saying something trite; split it, and 'Coin' is one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish dollar worth eight reales was the pirate's treasure coin, and literally a fraction of a group of eight.

clue.text: Doctor cures most clients

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician heals most of their patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers are people who buy services or goods, synonyms for patrons.

clue.text: Pupils study these citizens

definitions.meaning: school disciplines such as maths and history
the people living under a monarch's rule

explanation.definitionFit: Topics taught at school and people owing allegiance to a ruler share this word.

clue.text: Individual is tense after day in court

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the day letter

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous after a day in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means separate and recognisably different, as each one is unique.

clue.text: I ensure visit's arranged for where students might want to attend

definitions.text: where students might want to attend

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent promises to set up a campus tour for their teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "visit's" stands for 'is', a link word, and is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Institutions of higher learning are places school leavers hope to be admitted to study.

clue.text: Under pressure I almost pinched gun

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: stole means pinched or took

explanation.surface: Under stress, a confession of stealing a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun.

clue.text: Admitted a craving

parts.note: greed is a desire or craving

explanation.surface: A confession of a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted in the sense of conceded or accepted a point, consented.

clue.text: Shoots aircraft

definitions.meaning: spurts or streams forcefully, as water from a hose

explanation.definitionFit: Spurts of liquid and jet-powered planes share this word in its two senses.

clue.text: Worrying about the Queen with scamming going round

indicators.note: the swindling word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: conning means swindling or scamming
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about
ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: It is troubling that the monarch is surrounded by fraudsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link word but is the abbreviation circa; 'going round' says the scamming word wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concerning is troubling or alarming, causing anxiety.

clue.text: Discover animal sitting on church

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature is found perched on a church roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone is to discover them in the act, to spot them.

clue.text: Rise and fall of the sea temperature above fish

definitions.text: Rise and fall of the sea

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: Ocean levels and warmth have consequences for marine life.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular ebb and flow of ocean water driven by the moon.

clue.text: Europe perhaps happy restricting Northern Ireland, on reflection

indicators.note: the word for happy hems in the next piece

parts.note: content means satisfied or happy

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: A political musing about Europe and Northern Ireland, perhaps post-Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the great landmasses of the world, an example of the category.

clue.text: Sleep regularly abandoned after bird's call

indicators.note: the kept letters come after the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: every other letter of the word sleep is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A bird's song wakes someone, ending their sleep at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' looks like birdsong but is the verb: to name.
explanation.definitionFit: To title someone or something is to name it, to give it a designation.

clue.text: Crossword compilers — we're barking?

definitions.meaning: the people who write cryptic puzzles
the dogs called ... might say this of themselves: a breed of gundog

explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' also means mad, a wry self-description by puzzle writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzle compilers are called this, and so is a breed of gundog that barks.

clue.text: Crowded hospital confused no head of medicine

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: muddled means confused

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A busy ward is chaotic, with no senior doctor in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: People who huddled pressed close together in a crowd, as for warmth.
